newsitem.title: USA: Three die in U.S. collision of ultralight planes.
newsitem.headline: Three die in U.S. collision of ultralight planes.

text.p: Two ultralight aircraft collided in mid-air, spiraled to the ground and burst into flames on Thursday, killing the three occupants, officials said.
Local news reports said two of the victims were instructors and the third was a student pilot.

The two aircraft took off from Arlington airport, about 50 miles north of Seattle. They were flying in formation, one above the other, according to Jan Jorgensen, a spokeswoman for the Snohomish County Sheriff's Department.
Witnesses told authorities that the ultralights collided and crashed in a pea field near Arlington, Jorgensen said, about 500 yards from Interstate 5, a busy freeway, she added.
Three men in the two planes were killed, Jorgensen said. She said authorities were not releasing the names of the men, who were so badly burned that dental records would be needed to identify them.
Local news reports said two of the victims were veteran instructors and the third a student pilot. An ultralight flying club is based at Arlington airport, Jorgensen said.
The cause of the collision was unknown and was under investigation by the sheriff's department, Jorgensen said.
